How Windows decides which rule wins
When your changes actually show up

The mistakes that trip people up
How Group Policy fits with Intune and Azure

takeaways: Group Policy lets an admin define a rule once in a GPO and have every domain-joined Windows machine apply it, with the setting closest to the user or computer usually winning.
Changes arrive on a refresh schedule rather than instantly, and most trouble comes from sprawl, untested rollouts, blocked inheritance and missing documentation.
Devices joined only to Microsoft Entra ID do not process Group Policy, so Intune and Group Policy Analytics take over in the cloud while both run side by side in hybrid setups.
hook: The long password, the drive that appears on its own and the settings you cannot touch on your work laptop usually come from Group Policy. This plain-language episode is for anyone new to Windows administration who wants to understand how GPOs are applied, why changes seem slow, and how Group Policy relates to Intune and Microsoft Entra ID.
